detect-names-and-quotes-no-score:
Yes, heavily. Line by line:

- **"In today's fast-paced digital landscape"** — banned opener (E5), stacked with "landscape" itself being AI vocabulary (B1).
- **"isn't just a tool - it's a partner"** — negative parallelism (B3), the single most reliable tell there is. Also an em dash standing in for a hyphen.
- **"stands as a testament to"** — copula avoidance (B2) plus significance inflation (A1) in one phrase. Nothing "stands as" anything; it just *is* something, and the sentence won't say what.
- **"pivotal"** — AI vocabulary (B1), and it's modifying "commitment," which is already vague.
- **"seamless, vibrant collaboration"** — brochure adjectives (A4). Neither word is doing descriptive work; they're mood lighting.
- **"empowering teams to unlock their full potential"** — vague declarative (A7) dressed as a benefit. It asserts value without naming a single thing the platform does.

Underneath all that, there's no actual content: no feature, no claim, no specific outcome. That's the real tell, not just the vocabulary. Strip the inflation and there's nothing left to rewrite, because nothing was said in the first place.

Dear Orla,

I'm Dan, and I run ScentVerdict, a fragrance review site I started last year after getting frustrated with how hard it was to find honest reviews of niche perfumes.

Every review is based on at least two weeks of wear, with longevity, projection and value scored separately, because a single star rating hides too much. We have published 2,400 reviews over the past twelve months, and our readers tell us the separate scores are why they keep coming back.

I have been following your house for a while, and I think your approach to small-batch releases is exactly the kind of story our readers care about. I would love to review your autumn collection, and I am happy to share more on our methodology: how we handle samples, how we disclose free products, and how we keep reviews independent of any commercial relationship.

We also run a monthly newsletter for our most engaged readers, plus a growing presence on Instagram and TikTok, where our short wear-test videos have done particularly well.

If this sounds interesting, I would be glad to set up a call at a time that suits you.

Kind regards,
Dan
